title: Chapter 128 — Active Listening & Empathy
intro: Most service failures are not product failures — they are listening failures.

sections.title: Active Listening Techniques
sections.content:
Let the customer finish before responding. The mirror: repeat the last 2-3 words they said as a question — they elaborate without you asking. The pause: wait 2 seconds before responding — shows you are thinking. The summary: 'So what I am hearing is...' — confirms understanding.

Paraphrase back what you heard. 'So the dishwasher started leaking on Tuesday and your kitchen floor got wet' tells them you listened. Jumping straight to 'I will file a warranty claim' tells them you are processing them, not hearing them.

sections.title: Empathy That Doesn't Sound Scripted
sections.content:
'I understand how frustrating that must be' sounds scripted because it is. Better: 'If my brand new dishwasher leaked on my kitchen floor, I would be calling too.' Personal. Real. Connected.

Empathy is not agreement. You can empathize without admitting fault. 'I can see why you feel that way' acknowledges their emotion without promising a specific resolution.

The person who feels heard is already halfway to satisfied, even before you solve the problem.

sections.title: Reading Between the Lines
sections.content:
The customer who says 'everything is fine' in a flat tone is not fine. The customer who says 'I guess it is okay' has a complaint they are not voicing. The customer who asks 'is this normal?' is worried but not angry yet.

Listen for tone changes, hesitation, and qualifying words. When you hear them: 'I noticed you paused there — is there something that is not sitting right?' That question opens the real conversation.
